s1loc: Oldham Foodbank runs within the Trussell network, getting emergency parcels to people in crisis across the borough, while FareShare Greater Manchester redistributes surplus food to hundreds of charities, community centres and breakfast clubs from its volunteer-run warehouse. Action Together is the local infrastructure body, connecting people to volunteer roles and supporting voluntary, community and faith groups across Oldham, Rochdale and Tameside, with community development workers covering districts such as Chadderton and Werneth.

The sector here runs at every size. National charities and regional names with shop chains and central buying sit alongside small community groups, neighbourhood pantries, faith-run foodbanks and volunteer-led projects working on a shoestring across Failsworth, Chadderton, Werneth and the town centre. Dr Kershaw's Hospice funds its care through a string of shops and the Furniture Hub off Shaw Road. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the larger names and direct online with no minimum for the smallest group.

Dr Kershaw's Hospice has added quality to life-limiting care since 1989 and leans on volunteers to run its shops, sorting donations, steaming clothes and serving customers. Action Together's volunteering officers match local people to roles across All About Oldham's wide directory of community organisations, and mutual-aid and neighbourhood groups across Chadderton, Failsworth and Werneth keep parcels and warm spaces going. From the Trussell parcel line to a single church hall handing out tea, the borough's volunteers cover a real spread of need on modest budgets.

s1loc: The Brick is one of Wigan's best-known charities, running the borough's largest food bank plus a Food Community laid out like a shop where members choose items for a small fee, alongside crisis intervention and debt support. Its volunteers make up parcels and drive vans collecting donations from supermarkets across the Wigan and Leigh borough. FareShare Greater Manchester backs the wider picture, moving surplus food to community groups, while Wigan and Leigh Hospice anchors local fundraising and care.

The sector here runs at every size. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the larger names and direct online with no minimum for the smallest group.

Wigan and Leigh Hospice runs charity shops in Ashton, Atherton, Golborne, Hindley, Leigh, Pemberton, Standish and Shevington, all leaning on volunteers who give their time to fund hospice care. Sue Ryder also trades in Pemberton, and The Brick's growing Food Community is shifting the borough from emergency parcels toward dignity and choice. Volunteer drivers, parcel-packers and shop teams across Hindley, Pemberton and the town centre keep these projects running, covering a genuine spread of need on tight community budgets.

The Sutton Coldfield Charitable Trust, the Royal Sutton Coldfield Town Council and Age Concern Birmingham work with voluntary, community and faith organisations to support residents in need. The Lincolnshire Community Foundation has awarded over twenty-five million pounds to charities and community groups across Greater Lincolnshire since 2002, and the Greater Lincolnshire Food Partnership ties local foodbanks together with FareShare for bulk redistribution.

St Barnabas Hospice supports more than twelve thousand people a year across Lincolnshire and calls volunteers its life-blood, staffing two dozen shops with friendly teams who need no experience. The Acts Trust runs the foodbank with delivery drivers, warehouse and serving volunteers, the Lincolnshire Community and Voluntary Partnership helps groups find funding, and mutual-aid projects across Sincil Bank, Ermine and Boultham keep parcels and warm spaces going. st helens.s1_head: St Helens' charity and volunteer sector

FareShare Merseyside redistributes surplus food to more than two hundred charities and community groups across Merseyside and the Wirral, run by a team of almost a hundred volunteers picking, packing and driving deliveries.

The sector here runs at every size. Willowbrook Hospice offers retail volunteering across its shops, where teams meet customers, sort donations, steam clothing and serve at the till. Member-led pantries in Thatto Heath, West Park, Eccleston, Newton-le-Willows, Sutton, Moss Bank, Haydock and Billinge let members pay a small subscription and choose groceries, covering a real spread of need on tight budgets.
